rows.text:
The Gemma B70 decode benchmark evaluates autoregressive throughput and latency under varying KV cache pressures. To establish a reliable benchmark, the testbed utilizes a fixed prompt length to isolate the decode benchmark phase from the prefill benchmark phase. During the decode benchmark, the primary metric is tokens per second (TPS), which serves as the core benchmark for hardware utilization. 

A critical component of the decode benchmark is the memory bandwidth bottleneck; as the model scales, the decode benchmark performance becomes increasingly bound by HBM throughput rather than compute TFLOPS. To ensure the benchmark remains consistent, the benchmark environment must account for quantization effects, as INT8 or FP8 precision will shift the decode benchmark results compared to BF16. 

Furthermore, the decode benchmark must analyze the impact of batch size on total throughput. While increasing batch size improves the aggregate decode benchmark score, it simultaneously increases per-token latency, a trade-off central to any production-grade decode benchmark. Consequently, the final decode benchmark report should provide a Pareto frontier of latency versus throughput to fully characterize the Gemma B70 decode benchmark performance.
